doc.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Family Carnegie Hall concert and Billy Taylor's praise
summary: Laws recalls the Carnegie Hall concert with his siblings and a big band and Billy Taylor's compliments.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: I remember Billy Taylor was so excited about that record, because I remember we did a Carnegie Hall concert. I had Debra and Eloise and Ronnie. They all played on it. Had a big band, because CBS sponsored the – all these instruments. I had trumpets and trombones, because that’s what’s on that record. They supported strings. Back then, that’s when the record companies got behind supporting you with additional instruments and all that. I never will forget, boy, people in the aisle just rocking with that song. Billy Taylor came to the dressing room and said, “Man, that was a tremendous piece.” He complimented me on that. That meant a lot to me, because, you know, Billy Taylor’s a bebopper.
Oh yeah, but you know he’s got that other side where he said I Wish I Knew How It Would Feel to Be Free.
